content.title: 'NCIS' Kills Off a Major Character in the Show's 500th Episode. The Actor Reacts
content.text: The 500th episode of “NCIS” definitely wasn’t one to forget.The long-running CBS series killed off a major character on the March 24 episode when Director Leon Vance, played by Rocky Carroll, died in a shooting with a corrupt agent as part of a plot to shut down NCIS. After the shooting, Vance has a vision of a young Dr. Ducky Mallard (played by Adam Campbell) before dying. Ducky was an original “NCIS” character played by David McCallum, who died in 2023.Showrunner Steven D. Binder hatched the idea of killing off Vance on the episode. Rocky Carroll as NCIS Director Leon Vance.CBS Photo Archive / CBS via Getty Images“It seems like all hope is gone. But fortunately, Director Vance is able to get to the bottom of this plan and save the agency,” Carroll told USA Today about what Binder told him. “And in the process of saving the agency, he loses his life.”“I said, ‘Repeat that last part again,’” Carroll said about the conversation with Binder. “I’m sitting there having this out-of-body experience because I’ve been told we’re going to have this episode basically centered around the death of this character. It dawned on me that we’ve just finally come to that road.”He’s amazed that no one knew Vance’s death was coming.“I think it’s gonna be a huge shock for people,” he told Variety. I’ve been able to wrap my mind around it and come to terms with it because I’ve known about this since November, when I was first told about what was going to happen.”Carroll, a veteran actor who has also enjoyed runs on “Chicago Hope,” “The Agency” and “Roc,” says Vance’s fate was wonderfully done.“I’ve been able to kind of come full circle with it. And I really think it’s a great episode,” he said.“NCIS” is currently in its 23rd season and Carroll joined the show during its fifth season in 2008. According to IMDB, he has been on 392 episodes. Carroll marvels at the run he has gotten to enjoy.“For selfish reasons, I have to remind people: I’ve been a character on this series for 18 years. Most Hollywood careers don’t last 18 years,” he said. “So to be able to play one character on one of the most popular shows in the world for 18 seasons, that’s the equivalent of living to be 105. You know, if you’ve known somebody who lived to be 105, when you go to that funeral, there’s a part of you that’s like, ‘OK, yeah, this is sad, but I mean, geez! The guy lived to be 105.’ So I feel that way with my character.”Carroll also appreciates that he got to portray Vance for as long as he did.“Look, if this had happened in my third season playing this character, I’d be devastated,” he said. “But if somebody had told me 18 years ago, ‘Here’s the deal: We’re gonna hire you to play this character. We’re gonna give you 18 consecutive seasons of work on the most watched show in the world. At the end of season 18, something’s gonna happen to your character. Will you accept this offer?’ — there’s not a single actor on the planet who wouldn’t say, ‘Oh, hell yeah. Sign me up. Eighteen years of work. Are you kidding me?’”
